---
title: "Relations"
---

A relation records which ordered pairs from two sets are related.

::: {#def-relation name="Relation" .definition}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. A *relation* over $X \times Y$ is a subset $R \subseteq X \times Y$.

If $Y=X$, the relation is called *homogeneous*. When $(x,y)\in R$, we say that $x$ is related to $y$ and write $xRy$.
:::

The definition in @def-relation treats a relation as a set of ordered pairs. Equivalently, its indicator is a proposition-valued function of two arguments.

::: {#exm-basic-relations name="Basic relations" .example}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be sets. The following are standard examples:

1. The *discrete relation* $X\times Y$.
2. The *empty relation* $\emptyset\subseteq X\times Y$.
3. When $Y=X$, the *diagonal relation* $\{(x,x):x\in X\}$.
:::

::: {#exr-equal-canonical-relations name="Equality of the basic relations" .exercise}
Give a necessary and sufficient condition for the empty, discrete, and diagonal relations to be equal.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution

Assume the three are homogeneous relations on the same set $X$, so $Y=X$. They are equal if and only if $X=\emptyset$.

If $X=\emptyset$, then

$$
X\times X=\emptyset
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\{(x,x):x\in X\}=\emptyset,
$$

so all three relations coincide. Conversely, if the diagonal relation is empty, then $X$ has no elements: any $x\in X$ would make $(x,x)$ an element of the diagonal. Therefore $X=\emptyset$.
:::
:::

::: {#exr-product-relation-subset name="Product of relations" .exercise}
Let $(X_1,R_1)$ and $(X_2,R_2)$ be pairs of sets and relations on them. The rule

$$
(x,y)\,(R_1\times R_2)\,(x',y')
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
xR_1x'\text{ and }yR_2y'
$$

defines a relation $R_1\times R_2$ on $X_1\times X_2$. Express this relation as a subset of $(X_1\times X_2)^2$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution

The relation is

$$
R_1\times R_2
=
\left\{
\bigl((x,y),(x',y')\bigr)\in(X_1\times X_2)^2
:
(x,x')\in R_1\text{ and }(y,y')\in R_2
\right\}.
$$
:::
:::
